result: The authors demonstrate that individual cerebellar granule cells receive convergent inputs from both the external cuneate nucleus (ECN, carrying proprioceptive information) and the basilar pontine nucleus (BPN), establishing the multimodal nature of mammalian granule cells. Using genetic and viral tracing with synaptic resolution, they found that 40% of proprioceptive granule cells also receive BPN inputs.

The synaptic-resolution approach directly visualizes ECN and BPN inputs onto the same granule cells, addressing the long-standing controversy about granule cell multimodality.

result: The findings confirm predictions from the Marr-Albus theory that granule cells perform expansion recoding through multimodal mixing of mossy fiber inputs, supporting their proposed associative capacity.

This is a key prediction of the Marr-Albus model that had remained unconfirmed in mammals for nearly 50 years.
